## Purpose

This document builds a descriptive BMI summary by income group and gender in R, 
then checks it against a Python/pandas translation in `translation.ipynb`.

## Load the data

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
```

The data path is relative to the repository root. This works at render because `_quarto.yml` sets `execute-dir: project`.

```{r}
#| label: load-data
nhanes <- read_csv(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## Raw data checks

These match the inspection steps in the Python notebook and will inform `parity-table.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: raw-checks
nrow(nhanes)
ncol(nhanes)
names(nhanes)
sum(is.na(nhanes$BMI))
```

## Part A: R Pipeline

```{r}
#| label: part-a-pipeline
r_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), !is.na(Gender)) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 2),
    sd_bmi = round(sd(BMI), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(IncomeGroup, Gender)

r_summary
```

Checks for the parity table: rows left after the missingness filter, the number of grouped rows, and the stored rounded values. 
The tibble above prints only three significant digits, so the last two lines show the full two-decimal values

```{r}
#| label: part-a-checks
nrow(filter(nhanes, !is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), !is.na(Gender)))
nrow(r_summary)
r_summary$mean_bmi
r_summary$sd_bmi
```
